title: Asia’s Startup Funding At Near Record High In Q3, Driven By AI
key_facts: Investors put $38.5 billion into reported seed- through growth-stage financings for Asian startups in Q3 2026, per Crunchbase data.
About 55%, an estimated $21 billion, went to AI-focused companies.
Total funding is down substantially from Q2, which was boosted by a $7.4 billion financing for China's DeepSeek, but is still the second-highest tally on record.
China took roughly $27 billion, about 70% of the Asian total; India was second with $2.9 billion and Singapore third with $2.5 billion.

The largest round was Beijing-based foundation model company Moonshot AI's $3.5 billion in July at a reported $35 billion valuation; Kling AI, Kuaishou's generative video spinout, raised about $3 billion in July with Baidu and Tencent.
Seed and angel funding was $4.9 billion, up about 22% from Q2 and more than double a year earlier; Series A and B funding was $13.6 billion, down 28% from Q2 and up 65% from a year earlier.
Funding to startups in India and Singapore was down significantly from Q2.
Data is as of 5 Oct 2026 and based on reported deals; seed figures rise as data arrives after quarter end.

why_it_matters_hint: Asian venture money is concentrating on Chinese AI companies while India and Singapore fell back.
